node.name: Hatha Yoga (11/5)
node.descriptionText:
Join Karmen in the Yale Schwarzman Center Dance Studio (located on the lower level of YSC) for hatha yoga with an emphasis on the South Asian roots of the practice. Classes will include all areas of yogic study, practiced through movement, meditation, mantra, mudra, and breathwork, and are meant to be a guide for your personal practice.

Yoga mats will be provided but you are more than welcome and encouraged to bring your own. Please bring flexible clothes, a water bottle, and an openness to slowing down your breath and mind for 60 minutes! 

If you realize you cannot attend, please cancel your registration so that students from the waitlist may join. 

The Good Life Center is committed to making our events accessible to everyone. At your request, yoga instructors may be able to offer modifications for certain poses during your yoga class. If you require an accommodation or service to fully participate, please contact goodlifecenter@yale.edu.

node.name: Dinner Discussion: Xu Hanqing
node.descriptionText: Please join a YLS Paul Tsai China Center dinner with Senior Fellow Jamie Horsley and Professor Hanqing Xu, our Visiting Scholar and criminal defense lawyer qualified in China, with seven years of experience at Beijing Shangquan Law Firm. He specializes in complex criminal cases, including violent crime, financial crime, and cybercrime. He holds an MSc in Criminology and Criminal Justice from the University of Oxford, where his research focused on transitional justice, the death penalty, and the politics of crime control. We hope you can join us for this discussion!

node.name: Treasures from the Yale Film Archive: THE MURDER OF FRED HAMPTON + MAY DAY x 4
node.descriptionText:
THE MURDER OF FRED HAMPTON (Howard Alk, 1971, 35mm, 88 mins)
MAY DAY x 4 (Brian Meacham, 2026, DCP, 35 mins)
Sampada Aranke and Brian Meacham in person! New print! Urgent, uncompromising, and essential, Alk’s acclaimed documentary captures history in the act, bringing us Hampton's extraordinary charisma and resolve along with the aftermath of the Chicago police raid that ended his life. The film is paired with the premiere of a new short that draws on archival footage from four separate productions that documented protests in early May, 1970, creating a kaleidoscopic portrait of the response to the New Haven Black Panther trials. 35mm print made with thanks to the UCLA Film & Television Archive. 35mm print and DCP from the Yale Film Archive.

The “Treasures from the Yale Film Archive” series is presented with support from Paul L. Joskow ‘70 M.Phil., ‘72 Ph.D.

node.name: Advanced Search Techniques
node.descriptionText: Learn skills to research like a librarian, including how to use "advanced search" techniques to find books and articles in Quicksearch.
node.descriptionHtml:
Learn skills to research like a librarian, including how to use "advanced search" techniques to find books and articles in Quicksearch. Join us for 30-minutes and get a step ahead for coursework and research projects!

Attendees will learn how to:

  • navigate to distinct resource types in Quicksearch (books, articles, etc.)

  • use filters (subject, author, discipline) to find more relevant results

  • identify Advanced Search features

  • broaden and narrow search results using operators AND, OR, and NOT

Audience: Undergraduate students. Graduate students are also welcome.

Students interested in this workshop might also be interested in “First Steps with Zotero” and "Demystifying the Literature Review." For individual support, reach out to your Personal Librarian or Subject Specialist Librarian.

Any student who attends at least 3 library workshops this semester will be eligible to receive a Yale Library tote bag! Learn more about the Workshop Incentive Program.

node.name: Push Party by Nia Akilah Robinson
node.descriptionText:
About the show: Nia Akilah Robinson’s Push Party is a lively ensemble comedy about six Black women trying to uphold fifteen years of friendship at a post-birthing party in Harlem. All Lelo wants is for this event to go smoothly, but tensions among the group rise and then explode when an unhoused person lands in the community room. Inspired by Black women’s stories of birth and motherhood and by the joys and challenges of life in Harlem, this new play confronts the moments when friendship erodes, when hope starts to falter, when we argue until we laugh, and when Black folk see other Black folk suffering and die a little inside.

Performance Dates and Times:
Thursday, November 5 @ 8pm 
Friday, November 6 @ 8pm 
Friday, November 6 @ 11pm 
Saturday, November 7 @ 4pm
Saturday, November 7 @ 8pm

node.name: The Story of My Life
node.descriptionText:
The Story of My Life follows the friendship of Alvin and Thomas, two men from a small town. These lifelong friends are reunited after Alvin’s mysterious death. In the abstract world of his mind, Thomas struggles to write Alvin’s eulogy while recounting the many turns that their lives have taken since meeting as children. Alvin searches through the manuscripts and stories in Thomas’ mind to lead him on a journey of remembrance. Through music and song, these two friends recount their adventures, explore their past dissonance and ultimately discover what is at the base of every strong friendship… love.

The Story of My Life is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI. www.mtishows.com

Produced with support from the Marc and Melissa Karetsky Family Theater Fund

node.name: Reading Strategies for Writing Papers
node.descriptionText:
Skip, skim, or read: most scholars don’t read every word, but which words do you choose? Learn strategies - that you can begin in the early research process - to efficiently select, read, and analyze a LOT of scholarly articles to prepare for a research paper.


Workshop Incentive Program: Any student who attends at least 3 library workshops this semester will be eligible to receive a FREE Yale Library tote bag. Learn more.
node.descriptionHtml:
Skip, skim, or read: most scholars don’t read every word, but which words do you choose? Learn strategies - that you can begin in the early research process - to efficiently select, read, and analyze a LOT of scholarly articles to prepare for a research paper.

Attendees will learn:

  1. Lateral reading – to make decisions about which articles to save for later
  2. Selective reading (aka skimming) – to identify the most important sections of a scholarly article
  3. Active reading – to ensure you maximize your time by reading with purpose

Audience: Undergraduate and graduate students in all disciplines.

Workshop Incentive Program: Any student who attends at least 3 library workshops this semester will be eligible to receive a FREE Yale Library tote bag. Learn more.

node.name: Teaching Across Disciplines with the Yale University Art Gallery’s Numismatics Collection: Thematic Approaches Across Disciplines
node.descriptionText:
The Yale University Art Gallery’s holdings of coins, paper money, tokens, and medals – the study of which is called numismatics – exceed in range and depth those found at any other university in North America. This workshop series focuses on the capacity of the Gallery’s global numismatics collection to support learning goals in any discipline or subject. Money Matters comprises three 90-minute thematic sessions that explore how numismatic objects across time and space can illuminate history, test or expand conceptual frameworks, and cultivate transferable skills. Providing participants with the exceptional opportunity to handle the art, these workshops aim to demystify the field of numismatics and foster an interdisciplinary appreciation of its role across the academic curriculum at Yale. Together with Gallery curators and Yale faculty members Prof. Joe Glynias (History), Prof. William Goetzmann (School of Management) and others, participants will brainstorm how to employ the objects meaningfully in their own teaching. 

The workshops (individually and as a series) are open to all Yale instructors of record, including tenured and tenure-track faculty, clinical instructional faculty, lecturers, lectors, and part-time acting instructors (PTAIs), as well as postdoctoral fellows and associates. 

Participants who attend at least two of the workshops are eligible to apply for curriculum development grants supported by the Faculty of Arts and Sciences to integrate the Gallery’s numismatics collection in their courses at Yale. Up to five grants of $1,500 each (paid as research funds) will be awarded. 

The workshops are hosted by Benjamin Hellings, the Jackson-Tomasko Associate Curator of Numismatics, and Liliana Milkova, the Nolen Curator of Education and Academic Affairs, and feature hands-on work and short teaching demos by Yale faculty. Please note that attendance is capped at 18 and registration is required. 

Fri., Oct. 9, 10-11:30 am	 	Physical Objects and Cultural Documents (https://cglink.me/2dA/r2325705)
Fri., Nov. 6, 10-11:30 am	 	Thematic Approaches Across Disciplines (https://cglink.me/2dA/r2325706)
Fri., Dec. 11, 10-11:30 am	Science, Technology, Networks (https://cglink.me/2dA/r2325707)

Prior to attending their first workshop, participants are invited to watch these short videos:
1.	Benjamin Hellings and Emily Pearce Seigerman on the Bela Lyon Pratt Gallery of Numismatics (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jG5ij-IOCuA&list=PLqJmQZgy9f_e3qEd8rxUefCMuJYflnJoc&index=10)
2.	Emily Pearce Seigerman on How to Read Coinage (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f04rj3rRtHI&list=PLqJmQZgy9f_e3qEd8rxUefCMuJYflnJoc&index=2)

node.name: Daily Worship and Communion at Marquand Chapel
node.descriptionText:
Join us at 11:30am in Marquand Chapel for our daily worship.

Worship in Marquand often draws on a wide variety of inherited Christian traditions, with the worship of many denominations being represented. Beyond that, though, we also pay attention to the rising number of people in Western society who have a lively interest in spirituality but feel no connection to traditional forms of church and worship. So Marquand is also actively engaged in original, creative, and experimental forms of worship, both for committed Christians and for those exploring the faith.
